topIssues.description: Consistently omits asymptomatic presentation information in medical QA responses
Fails to adapt explanation depth to user's indicated expertise level
Over-qualifies statements with excessive hedging in straightforward factual responses

keyLearnings: Medical QA responses systematically omit 'negative space' clinical information — conditions that can be asymptomatic are not flagged as such
Model performs 23% better on structured output tasks (lists, tables) vs. free-form narrative responses
Multi-turn conversations show degraded accuracy after turn 5, suggesting context window management issues
Hindi-language medical responses show 22% lower accuracy than equivalent English responses
System prompt with explicit regulatory citations improves compliance by 45% over general instructions
The model consistently excels at differential diagnosis reasoning but struggles with treatment recommendation specificity
newMemoryRules: MEM-2026-0312: For healthcare domain — always address asymptomatic presentations when applicable
MEM-2026-0313: When user indicates expertise level — calibrate response depth accordingly
MEM-2026-0314: For multi-turn medical conversations — summarize key context every 3 turns
recommendations: Schedule targeted fine-tuning session for medical completeness, focusing on asymptomatic conditions and risk-factor-based screening recommendations
Review and update system prompt to include explicit instructions for handling different user expertise levels
Implement context summarization at 3-turn intervals for multi-turn conversations to prevent accuracy degradation
Prioritize Hindi-language medical QA training data augmentation to address the 22% accuracy gap
Consider structured output mode for complex medical information to leverage the model's 23% performance advantage
